title: Two kinds of matter
hook: Explore the evidence behind a cosmic question.

knows: Light and gravity help astronomers study the universe.
doesNotKnow: Ordinary matter can emit, absorb or scatter light. Dark matter is detected mainly through gravity, while its exact composition remains an open question.

misconception: A learner may choose: It is made entirely of visible stars
objective: Use the visual model to reason about: How does dark matter differ from ordinary luminous matter in astronomical observations?

claims.text: Question, correct answer and explanation: How does dark matter differ from ordinary luminous matter in astronomical observations? It is primarily inferred through gravitational effects. Ordinary matter can emit, absorb or scatter light. Dark matter is detected mainly through gravity, while its exact composition remains an open question.
Visual caption: Light traces only some mass. The SVG is a conceptual illustration, not measured data or a scale model.
